Axiom:
Allocate concrete next-unused PhaseIDs; placeholders are not valid written output. Every task-owned code finding, including a one-line bug, gets at least one concrete `fix` PhaseID and one dependent concrete `test` PhaseID. Multiple findings sharing one owner may share one Round, but none may bypass it.
**Two forms, chosen by whether the current Round is still open (D-20):** - **Round still open** (no `#### Round close` written yet) — append `#### P — re-run: ` blocks for the new fix/test phases inside that SAME `### Round N`. - **Round already closed** — `— re-run:` is not valid there; append a brand new `### Round N+1 — , fix: ` instead, with its own fix/test phase blocks. A write into an already-closed Round is invalid input regardless of form.
Either way, `PHASES_OVERVIEW` MUST gain one row per new PhaseID — the Execution Log alone is not read by the phase-graph/dependency checks:
``` | ID | Kind | Deps | Status | |--------|------|------|--------| | P | fix | — | [ ] | | P | test | P | [ ] | ```
Set ticket Meta Status → `[~] IN_PROGRESS` — this is what `sdd-log round` already sets when opening a new Round; do not write `[ ] TODO` instead, which reads as "not started" and would drift from the tracker row `sdd-check` compares it against. Update `Reopens: `. Sync tracker: the owning `*.3-tasks.md` row → `[~] IN_PROGRESS` (same value, not TODO); parent rollups (scope and `specs/3-tasks.md`) → adjust counts.
`✅ RESOLVED` after a blocker is a related but separate concern owned by the journal's Blocker Trail work, not this axiom.
